clue.text: One's lucky in races beyond a mile

indicators.note: beyond says the racing piece comes after the mile piece in the answer

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for mile
Ascot is the famous English racecourse and its race meeting

explanation.surface: Someone has a lucky streak at the races once the distance goes past a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, famous for Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring good luck to its owners.

clue.text: It's the minister's place to designate names

indicators.note: designate is read as de-sign-ate, the letters of the next word given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A clergyman's job description says he must name things.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a Presbyterian or other Nonconformist minister.

clue.text: Short of shot-guns

parts.note: a shotgun with its barrel cut down short is described with a woodworking phrase

explanation.definitionFit: A sawn-off shotgun has its barrel shortened by cutting, so the phrase describes a short gun.

clue.text: So greatly tempted, got into debt

parts.note: over means excessively, so greatly, as in over-eager
drawn means attracted or lured, as tempted is

explanation.surface: Someone was so tempted by the shops that they ended up in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: Having overdrawn an account means taking out more than is in it, so going into debt to the bank.

clue.text: Little credit goes to academic stream in crucial period

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit, as on a bank statement
the Isis is the stretch of the Thames flowing through Oxford, a university city

explanation.surface: A student's small loan arrives just as the term reaches its critical point.
explanation.walkthrough: The ISIS is the name for the River Thames at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of intense difficulty when a decisive turn must come.

clue.text: Fleet Street contained an awful mixture of types

indicators.note: contained says the jumbled type sits inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: RD, road, stands in for street here as a road abbreviation
pi (or pie) is printers' jargon for a heap of jumbled type

explanation.surface: Fleet Street, home of the old newspapers, held a terrible jumble of printing type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like part of Fleet Street, London's old newspaper district, but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift, nimble and quick-moving.

clue.text: Stout aunt's off to church

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of the relative are disordered

explanation.surface: A portly aunt sets off for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the aunt's build, but it is the definition; 'off' scrambles the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch, like stout, means firm, loyal and resolute in support.

clue.text: Somehow resent accepting small bribe

indicators.note: accepting says the shuffled letters take another piece inside them
somehow says the following word's letters are arranged in some way

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone resents being offered a little bribe yet takes it anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' shuffles the letters of 'resent', and 'accepting' wraps those shuffled letters round the Scottish word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or small payment offered to win someone over.

clue.text: Outstanding winter features

parts.note: figures built of snow stand outside in winter, so they are out-standing

explanation.definitionFit: Snow figures are a familiar sight of winter, always standing out of doors in gardens.

clue.text: One giving a talk — on radio?

definitions.meaning: a person who delivers a lecture or address
the loudspeaker through which a radio set sounds

explanation.definitionFit: A speaker is both an orator and the device that turns signals into sound.

clue.text: Unemployment act?

parts.note: posing as the title of a law, it means the act of sacking someone

explanation.definitionFit: A dismissal is the act of firing an employee, which leaves them out of work.

clue.text: Needed to retaliate if your opponent gets the first blow?

definitions.text: Needed to retaliate if your opponent gets the first blow?

parts.words: Needed to retaliate if your opponent gets the first blow?
parts.note: blow is read as a puff of breath, so the reply needs another breath

explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is renewed energy after tiredness, here imagined as the next gust after the first.

clue.text: Record a piece of music

definitions.meaning: a single sound of a given pitch in music

explanation.definitionFit: To note is to jot down; a note is also a single musical tone.

clue.text: Capital school — initially having first-class backing

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word school

parts.note: of can mean possessing, as in a man of means

indicators.note: backing says the first-class symbol is read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: A top-ranked school is backed to the hilt.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class; 'backing' reverses it. The blog suspects 'school initially' may be the initials of a school, but S plus OF works.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Mock the northern city's affectation

indicators.note: affectation is read as the letters being affected, that is altered

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the airs and graces of a city up north.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means imitation or fake, just as synthetic materials are artificial.

clue.text: Taking steps to protest for 31 days in Greek capital

parts.note: March is a month of 31 days

indicators.note: capital picks out the first letter of the word Greek

explanation.surface: Protesters spend a whole month demonstrating in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching means walking in procession, often as a demonstration of protest.

clue.text: Is it paid to, or bought from, a barman?

definitions.text: Is it paid to, or bought from, a barman?

parts.words: Is it paid to, or bought from, a barman?
parts.note: barman means both a barrister who is paid fees and a person serving drinks

explanation.walkthrough: In British law a refresher is an extra fee paid to a barrister for a long case; it is also a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher is both a barrister's daily fee in a lengthy trial and a refreshing drink.

clue.text: Greeks and Romans are different, for instance

indicators.note: different says the letters of the following word come out otherwise

explanation.surface: Greeks and Romans are not alike, to take one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancients are the peoples of classical antiquity, chiefly the Greeks and Romans.

clue.text: Huge semi built to house males

indicators.note: to house says the rearranged letters hold another piece inside
built says the letters of the house type are put together anew

parts.note: men are males

explanation.surface: A semi-detached house is constructed big enough to lodge some men.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, common in Britain; 'built' rearranges its letters and 'to house' puts the males inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large, enormous.

clue.text: Gift is just about a pound

indicators.note: about says the even-handed word goes round the pound sign

parts.note: fair means just, even-handed
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A present is fair value at about a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural talent or aptitude, a gift for something.

clue.text: Flourishes, as spring comes in

indicators.note: comes in says the leap piece enters the two-letter word

parts.note: a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Things flourish when the spring season arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to exist in great quantity, to thrive in plenty.

clue.text: Fraud that's little short of a disgrace

indicators.note: little short of says the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: shame is disgrace

explanation.surface: A swindle that is nearly scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little short of' drops the last letter from SHAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake or impostor, something fraudulent.

clue.text: More or less ran one huge conglomerate

indicators.note: conglomerate says the three words are mixed together into a mass

explanation.surface: A man roughly speaking ran a single enormous business group.
explanation.definitionFit: Near enough means approximately, close to being so.

clue.text: Words of love among sisters

indicators.note: among says the zero sits within the sisters

parts.note: nuns are sisters in a religious order
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Words of affection spoken in a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouns are a class of words naming things.

clue.text: Gather information alternately with the French

indicators.note: with places the remaining letter of the French article after the second letter of the information word
alternately says the letters of the two words take turns, the article's first letter after the first of the information word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
la is the French for the (feminine); its first letter goes after the first of the information word
the second letter of the French article goes after the second letter of the information word

explanation.surface: Collect facts, taking turns with the French.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN and LA are interleaved letter by letter: G, L, E, A, N. The grammar can only show this as two insertions of LA's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, originally leftover grain after the harvest.

clue.text: Kind of comedian to fail to keep a date?

definitions.meaning: a solo performer telling jokes before an audience

definitions.text: to fail to keep a date?
definitions.meaning: to leave someone waiting by not turning up

explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comic performs alone; to stand up a date is not to show.

clue.text: Risk getting left in church

parts.note: chance means risk, as in take a chance

explanation.surface: Someone takes a gamble on being abandoned at church.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, where clergy and choir sit.

clue.text: It's not chalk that's used to score in skittles

definitions.meaning: from the saying as different as chalk and the dairy product

definitions.text: that's used to score in skittles
definitions.meaning: in skittles a heavy wooden disc is thrown to knock pins down

explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is chalk's opposite in the idiom and the disc thrown in a game of skittles.

clue.text: Its bars could be for those that drink too much

definitions.text: Its bars could be for those that drink too much

parts.words: Its bars could be for those that drink too much
parts.note: bars means the iron bars of a cell, not pubs, though drunks may end up behind them

explanation.definitionFit: A jail has barred windows, and drunken offenders may be locked up in one.
